observations.finding: Scoped sockets can attach sandbox/app identity to a new Wayland connection. This can shrink custom attribution for launched or sandboxed clients, but the backend must still own trusted identity fallback when no scoped socket is present.
Foreign toplevel handles can carry enough lifecycle/listing signal to reduce custom surface discovery, subject to compositor support and metadata completeness.
No standard protocol in this probe provides synchronous per-surface input denial in the compositor input path.

Image copy capture can request capture of image sources including toplevels into client-provided buffers. This can move capture transport toward standard protocol support where the compositor exposes the required source objects.
No standard protocol in this probe provides authority for DE-controlled per-surface move/resize geometry.
No standard protocol in this probe provides Agora DE owned tiling zones, planner revisions, layout rule settings, classified command results, or backend-acknowledged placement semantics.
No standard protocol in this probe provides Agora DE workspace activation, output-scoped workspace state, stable workspace surface_order, and focus order semantics.
No standard protocol in this probe classifies Agora DE shell chrome, shell popups, transient/dialog policyClass, parentSurfaceId, or tiling exclusion policy.
No standard protocol in this probe connects governed desktop-entry launch results, launch completion classes, and trusted compositor surface ids.
Image copy capture can contribute capture transport, but installed Agora DE still needs product-level classification, expected shell/native pixels, artifact paths, and failure taxonomy.
No standard protocol in this probe provides Agora DE agent action routes, command result classes, layout labels, or overlay label semantics.
No standard protocol in this probe defines install, restart, recovery, kill-all, soak, or GitHub-gated verification operations.
